zh.summary: Cori Clinical 为申办方和 CRO 提供临床试验的“活蓝图”AI 工作区，把机构历史试验知识与外部监管情报汇入同一版本化记录，驱动方案、预算、申报与合规审查。
zh.judgment: 最关键的商业判断是：它卖的不是文档生成，而是“设计变更—成本—文件—变更单”的联动可追溯性；能否成立取决于客户是否愿意把历史试验数据交给它并据此定价。
zh.replaces: 替代以 Word 文档、邮件线程、会议纪要和电子表格拼凑的方案撰写、可行性评估、风险登记、投标报价与变更管理流程。
zh.segment: 临床试验设计与运营的 AI 工作区（面向申办方与 CRO）
zh.product: 公司披露的产品核心是 Knowledge Hub：把方案、RFP 和历史试验读入一个版本化记录，并映射到 CDISC USDM v4.0。其上有可行性、设计与 SoA、试验风险、投标与预算、监管包、合规审查、修订和决策记录等模块，各模块读取其他模块的决策并按任意顺序推进。官网强调“Cori 起草、临床团队决定”，每个字段标注来源是人、文件还是 Cori。范围限于试验启动前后的设计与文档工作，不替代 CTMS、RIM、eTMF 等系统记录。
zh.customer: 使用者是申办方的临床开发与运营团队，以及 CRO 的投标、定价和项目启动团队；付费者应为机构而非个人，但具体采购层级未披露。痛点高频且昂贵：国家与中心选择依赖少数人的记忆，设计成本与中心负担在后期才暴露，投标在时间压力下靠表格和经验定价，监管更新需逐份人工比对。CRO 侧还叠加变更单漏计导致的不可计费工作。
zh.workflow: 输入是客户自己的历史方案、预算、SOP、模板、RFP 以及外部试验注册库和监管指南。流程从可行性情景评分开始，选定设计与访视表后，预算按 SoA 推算，风险按可比试验的发生率与成本打分，随后在客户模板上起草方案、知情同意、各国申报包并做合规审查，发现项定位到具体段落并需人工签核。设计变更时，系统列出受影响的文件、成本与日期，并为 CRO 重拟变更单。
zh.business_model: 输入未披露定价页、计费单位或合同结构，无法判断是按席位、按试验还是按模块收费；研究缺口已标注 pricing。可条件式推断：由于强调每客户独立部署、区域托管与不用于训练模型，交付成本可能高于纯 SaaS，单位经济是否成立取决于单客户试验数量与模块使用深度，此为推断而非已验证。
zh.traction: 唯一可核实的采用信号是公司披露的 ISO/IEC 27001 认证、GxP 对齐与 EU/US/UK 数据驻留，以及官网展示的示例研究界面；这些是公司自述，不是审计结论。输入中没有客户案例、付费客户数、留存或收入数据，research_gaps 标注 customer_case 与 documentation，因此不能把融资或认证当作需求验证。
zh.moat: 相对通用模型，其差异在于把机构私有历史试验、外部注册库与监管文本绑定到同一可追溯记录，并让预算、文件与变更单随设计联动；这需要领域数据结构和合规工作流，而非单纯生成能力。壁垒条件是客户愿意持续沉淀历史试验数据并接受其评分逻辑；若通用模型加客户自建检索即可覆盖，或客户不愿共享历史数据，护城河会显著变薄。
zh.funding_read: 本轮为 Seed，金额与原币由确定性层给出，投资方名单不等于领投名单。该阶段说明产品已从概念走到可演示的多模块工作区，并具备安全认证叙事，但资金支持本身不证明需求、收入或留存。下一里程碑应是公开可核验的付费客户案例与模块使用深度；资金用途未披露，须注明未知。
zh.risks: 第一，临床文档错误或遗漏的代价极高，若起草内容在合规审查中被发现系统性偏差，客户信任与责任风险会迅速放大。第二，客户历史试验数据是核心输入，若数据迁移、隐私审批或区域部署摩擦过大，采用会停在演示阶段。第三，CRO 与申办方对定价透明度的诉求可能冲突，产品若无法同时服务两侧，商业化会被迫二选一。
zh.takeaway: 可借鉴的做法是把 AI 定位为“带来源标记的起草者”而非决策者，并把一次设计变更自动传导到成本、文件与变更单，让价值以可审计的联动而非生成速度呈现。另一可取之处是明确不替换客户既有系统记录，降低采购阻力。
zh.watch_next: 下一项可验证指标是是否出现具名客户案例及其使用模块范围；同时应关注定价页是否公开、是否披露按试验或按席位的计费方式，以及是否有第三方对文档准确率的评估。

en.summary: Cori Clinical offers sponsors and CROs an AI workspace that builds a living blueprint of a clinical trial, combining an organisation's prior trial knowledge with external regulatory intelligence in one versioned record that drives protocol, budget, submission and compliance work.
en.judgment: The key commercial question is whether customers will treat it as a traceable design-to-cost-to-document system rather than a document generator, and whether they will entrust historical trial data to it for pricing.
en.replaces: Word documents, email threads, meeting notes and spreadsheets used for protocol drafting, feasibility, risk registers, bid pricing and change-order management.
en.segment: AI workspace for clinical trial design and operations (sponsors and CROs)
en.product: The company-reported core is a Knowledge Hub that reads protocols, RFPs and past trials into one versioned record mapped to CDISC USDM v4.0. Modules cover feasibility and strategy, design and SoA, trial risks, bid and budget, regulatory package, compliance review, amendments and decision records; each reads what the others decided and can run in any order. The site stresses that Cori drafts while the clinical team decides, and that every value shows whether a person, a file or Cori supplied it. Scope is design and documentation around trial start and conduct, not a replacement for CTMS, RIM, eTMF or document systems.
en.customer: Users are sponsor clinical development and operations teams and CRO bid, pricing and study-startup teams; the paying entity is presumably the organisation, though the buying level is not disclosed. Pain is frequent and expensive: country and site choices rest on a few people's memory, design cost and site burden surface late, bids are priced under time pressure from spreadsheets, and regulatory updates are checked by hand. CROs additionally lose unbillable work when scope changes are missed.
en.workflow: Inputs are the customer's own prior protocols, budgets, SOPs, templates and RFPs plus external trial registries and regulatory guidance. The flow starts with scored feasibility scenarios; once design and visit schedule are chosen, the budget is projected from the SoA, risks are scored on how often and how costly they appeared in comparable trials, and the protocol, consent form, country packs and submission documents are drafted on customer templates and checked against ICH GCP, applicable regulations and SOPs. Findings are pinned to passages and require human sign-off. On a design change, affected documents, costs and dates are listed, and CROs get a redrafted change order.
en.business_model: The input contains no pricing page, billing unit or contract structure, so it is not possible to tell whether it charges per seat, per trial or per module; this is recorded as a pricing research gap. A conditional inference, not verified, is that per-customer deployments with regional hosting and no training on customer data may raise delivery costs above pure SaaS, so unit economics depend on trials per customer and module depth.
en.traction: The only verifiable adoption signals are company-reported ISO/IEC 27001 certification, GxP alignment and EU/US/UK data residency, plus sample study screens on the site; these are company claims, not audit conclusions. The input has no named customer cases, paying customer counts, retention or revenue, and research gaps flag customer_case and documentation, so neither funding nor certification should be read as demand validation.
en.moat: Versus general-purpose models, the difference is binding an organisation's private trial history, external registries and regulatory text into one traceable record where budget, documents and change orders follow design changes; that requires domain data structures and compliance workflow, not just generation. The moat holds only if customers keep depositing historical trial data and accept its scoring logic; if general models plus customer-built retrieval suffice, or customers refuse to share history, it thins considerably.
en.funding_read: The round is Seed, with amount and native currency rendered by the deterministic layer; the investor list is not a lead-investor list. The stage suggests the product has moved from concept to a demonstrable multi-module workspace with a security certification narrative, but funding does not prove demand, revenue or retention. The next milestone should be publicly verifiable paying customer cases and module depth; use of proceeds is undisclosed and must be marked unknown.
en.risks: First, errors or omissions in clinical documents are very costly; systematic drafting deviations found in compliance review would quickly damage trust and raise liability. Second, historical trial data is the core input, so heavy friction in data migration, privacy approval or regional deployment could stall adoption at the demo stage. Third, CRO and sponsor interests in pricing transparency may conflict, forcing the company to choose one side if it cannot serve both.
en.takeaway: A transferable practice is positioning AI as a source-marked drafter rather than a decision-maker, and making one design change propagate automatically to cost, documents and change orders so value shows up as auditable linkage rather than generation speed. Explicitly not replacing customers' systems of record is another way to lower procurement resistance.
en.watch_next: The next verifiable indicator is whether named customer cases appear and which modules they use; also watch whether a pricing page is published, whether billing is per trial or per seat, and whether any third party assesses document accuracy.
